scenes.heading: Understanding file formats and deliverables clients actually need

sents.d: Understanding file formats and deliverables clients actually need
Delivering the wrong files creates unnecessary back-and-forth after a project ends.
Many designers deliver only a flattened image file, then get a follow-up request days later for an editable or print-ready version — clarifying deliverables upfront avoids this entirely.

A typical complete delivery includes an editable source file, a high-resolution version for print, a web-optimized version, and for logos specifically, versions in different color modes (full color, black, white) and formats (vector and raster).
Listing exactly which files will be delivered in the contract or proposal — not just 'final files' — sets a clear, checkable expectation for both sides.

take: List exactly which files you'll deliver.
